# Plain C# baseline on the same tasks
<!-- GENERATED from the Phrase Board (issue #86, sha256:750a65c940bf8db41b390785f32892a0a94eff4f5162a09f8a8f74b6a424def4). Do not edit this file: edit the issue. -->


- **Status:** Ready (rank: see `C:\Users\ringe\projects\phrase-lang\board\MILESTONE-usable-v1.md`, read-only)
- **Shape:** Story
- **Type:** feature (thin slice; a measurement)
- **Milestone:** Measure first: does Phrase beat plain C# on tokens and attempts at an equal or better pass rate?
- **Source:** Steve's priority ruling, 2026-10-26 (an outside assessment of what Phrase is worth): the question that decides everything is whether models finish real tasks with fewer tokens and attempts in Phrase than in plain C# using the same libraries, at an equal or better pass rate; nothing has measured that yet. Team plan: Decider D31 (Codex, Copilot, Grok Support-it; agy no response). Pre-registered bar: Decider D32, recorded BEFORE any result row.
- **Depends on:** none
- **Story:** As Riley, I want the same development tasks written as plain C# with the same libraries and the same observable outcomes as tests, so that I can see Phrase's pass rate, attempts and tokens against the fair baseline before the emitter costs more.
- **Hypothesis (pre-registered):** We believe a plain C# baseline will show whether Phrase has room to win on tokens and attempts. We will know when N=5 scheduled runs per model record pass rate, attempts and total tokens (documentation included) on write tasks and on change tasks, and the little-room gate has fired or not, before any Phrase head-to-head row exists. Frozen bar (Decider D32, amended after the seats' changes, recorded BEFORE any result): N = 5 SCHEDULED runs per model per task (harness-error rows stay in the count); attempt cap 3 (a run that never passes counts as 3 attempts and a fail); EVERY run is scored and a failed run is charged the tokens it consumed through attempt 3; means are task-macro averages (each task weighs the same); pass rate is the unweighted mean of per-model rates; pass rate: Phrase within 5 points of plain C# or better is WIN-eligible, 5 to 10 points worse is a TIE, worse than 10 points is a LOSS, and a read-task gap worse than 10 points blocks WIN; Phrase mean total tokens (documentation and cheat-sheet tokens INCLUDED, charged on every attempt) at most 75 percent of C# on tasks passing in both arms, on write tasks AND, separately, on change tasks; Phrase mean attempts at most the C# mean on each of those groups; patch rate 0: a run that goes green only by editing the generated C# counts as a Phrase fail and any patch share above 0 blocks WIN; fewer than 3 models, fewer than 3 paired task-runs in a group, or more than 10 percent harness-error rows makes the call INCONCLUSIVE; a write-only saving is a TIE; the holdout (3 tasks written outside the mob: one write, one change, one that fits no pattern; hashes recorded before the first scored run) is judged on the same bar and a holdout that is INCONCLUSIVE makes the whole call INCONCLUSIVE; the result is exactly one of WIN, LOSS, TIE, INCONCLUSIVE with absolute pass rates beside it. Frozen with the bar: model versions, prompts, context limits, task hashes, timeouts, token accounting and the retry policy. Little-room gate: if every included model is at 90 percent pass rate or more and 2 mean attempts or fewer on plain C#, and change-task tokens are at most 2 times write-task tokens, the emitter chain pauses for one Decider. A later change to any number is a new Decider and voids stored rows.
- **Acceptance criteria (Given/When/Then; at most 3, each failing on partial work):**
  1. Given the eight development tasks, When the C# suite runs, Then each task checks the same observable outcome as its Phrase twin through xUnit, uses FastEndpoints only when the outcome is an HTTP endpoint, and the prompt contains no Phrase docs (the check fails if the outcome set differs)
  2. Given N=5 scheduled runs for each of the four models, When the run finishes, Then each row records pass, attempts, tokens in, tokens out, measurement mode and kind (write or change), and the little-room gate result is written on the card (the check fails if any field is missing)
  3. Given three sealed holdout hashes recorded before the run, When the run finishes, Then those bodies have no rows (the check fails if a holdout was opened or scored)

## Context

- Files: a new bench/csharp-baseline tree and its own runner; it does not edit tools/Phrase.Bench, so 084, 085 and 086 stay parallel. Specs as tests do not need Phrase (Gherkin with Reqnroll, or xUnit with Given/When/Then names, already give C# verifiable output): the fair baseline is C# plus the same libraries plus the same specs as tests, so any Phrase win must come from vocabulary and compression. Run FIRST among the measurements: if C# already nears 100 percent at low cost, Phrase has little room to win. Holdouts are written OUTSIDE the mob (a person who will not drive or review 086 to 088 writes three tasks: one write, one change, one that fits no pattern); only their hashes enter the record before this card starts.
- Safety rules apply in full. Bootstrap phase: the pre-registered bar is fixed by Decider before results; numbers inform, nothing is kept or reverted on results alone.
